ashby:1password:a6f7a1ee-62c7-4d86-afe6-.summary: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

sections.title: About 1Password
paras: At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

Reporting to the Chief Business Officer, you will build and lead a scalable Partner Success organization for 1Password. You’ll define how partners onboard, build expertise, deliver customer value, and grow their businesses while shaping lifecycle programs, operating models, and measurable success outcomes. By helping partners deliver secure, reliable experiences for their customers, you’ll extend 1Password’s mission to more organizations.

sections.title: What we're looking for:
bullets: Bring 12+ years of experience in partner success, customer success, channel operations, or related roles in Business-to-Business (B2B) software, including experience leading teams and managing managers. Experience within an AI-forward organization is considered a strong asset.
Demonstrate success building or scaling a partner-facing organization with measurable improvements in partner productivity, customer retention, expansion, and satisfaction.
Understand partner business models, particularly managed service providers and resellers, including recurring revenue, service delivery, and the economics of a profitable partner practice.
Design lifecycle programs, partner segmentation, success plans, health scoring, and executive engagement across a diverse partner portfolio.
Apply strong commercial judgment and analytical skills to connect partner engagement and customer adoption with revenue outcomes and investment decisions.
Build trust with partner leaders, lead complex escalations, and influence priorities across Sales, Customer Success, Product, Marketing, Support, Operations, and Finance.

Translate strategy into repeatable processes, lead through change, and establish clear accountability in a growing organization; experience in cybersecurity, identity and access management, or another technically complex Software as a Service (SaaS) category is a plus.

sections.title: What you can expect:
paras: USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $256,000 USD and $384,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $240,000 CAD and $360,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Our culture
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first.

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone . Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

ashby:govwell:81a23971-e007-44db-9812-6d.summary:
We the people — and the taxpayers — deserve good government. Yet today, interacting with government services is often frustrating and inefficient. GovWell is building the AI operating system transforming how governments serve communities, starting with local agencies.

GovWell replaces legacy software for municipalities and counties, empowering public servants to radically streamline public services and cut internal processing time for permits and licenses by up to 95%.

Founded in 2023, GovWell powers 5,000+ mission-critical processes for agencies in 35+ states serving millions of residents. The company has raised $35M in funding from Insight Partners, Work-Bench, and Bienville Capital, and the team works in person at GovWell HQ in New York City. Read more about our founding story in TechCrunch .

sections.title: ☀️ Why GovWell?
bullets: A mission that matters: Building AI-powered products to fix outdated government systems isn’t just a technical challenge—it’s a historic opportunity to improve our foundational relationship with government and ensure trillions of tax dollars result in high quality services. WATCH: Mission & Vision with CEO & Co-Founder Troy LeCaire

Real-world impact: GovWell’s product is the system of record for government services that affect millions of Americans. From streamlining permitting for small businesses to accelerating affordable housing development, your work will make an immediate difference.

Join a startup in hyper-growth: We’ve found product-market fit and are scaling the business very quickly (4X ARR growth in the last year). As an early team member, you’ll learn what it takes to build a successful startup. You’ll work closely with the founders while enjoying exceptional autonomy and ownership over your work.

sections.title: 🌟 Role overview
paras: When a city switches to GovWell, one thing has to go right before anything else can: their data. A decade of permits, parcels, inspections, and license records — often living in a 2009 Access database, a folder of CSVs, or a legacy system with no documentation — has to land in GovWell accurately. If it doesn't, our relationship with a new client is off to a bumpy start.

As a Data Solutions Engineer, you own that moment. You'll take whatever a city hands you — messy exports, inconsistent codes, half-mapped schemas, geospatial data of questionable quality — and turn it into clean, trusted production data. That means writing SQL/Python that finds the edge cases before they find you, leading calls with non-technical government staff, and making judgment calls on messy data that you'd stake the launch on.

You'll report directly to our Head of Data Solutions & Geospatial Products, Max Payson , and work across Deployment, Product and Engineering - with real influence over how GovWell's onboarding process matures as we scale.

sections.title: 💻 What you’ll do
bullets: Own data migrations end-to-end. Work directly with government staff to understand their source systems, configure schema mappings and ingestion settings, run validations and dry-runs, and ensure accurate, complete data lands in GovWell.

Be the gatekeeper for data quality. Identify gaps, inconsistencies, and edge cases in legacy data before they become production problems. Make documented judgment calls within defined constraints — and prevent bad or unsafe data from ever reaching production.

Be the technical face of onboarding. Lead customer calls, clearly explain data requirements and tradeoffs, and guide agency staff through the transition from legacy systems to GovWell with calm confidence.

Make the process better as you run it. Use internal tools, templates, and playbooks to reduce time-to-launch and minimize manual work. Help build toward a future where migrations are predictable, repeatable, and fast.

Close the feedback loop with Product and Engineering. Document recurring issues, unmet assumptions, and tooling gaps encountered during migrations — helping the platform evolve based on what you see in the field.

sections.title: Required
bullets: 2-4 years of hands-on experience in data migrations, ETL/ELT, technical implementations, or a closely related role working with messy, real-world production data.

Demonstrated ability to work directly in a Python codebase day-to-day (reading, debugging, and shipping changes via PRs) — ideally in a data/pipeline repo (e.g., Airflow DAGs, ingestion jobs, migration utilities).
Strong SQL proficiency used in practice for analysis, validation, reconciliation, and transformation work.
Experience translating ambiguous stakeholder requirements into concrete, testable migration/implementation plans (what we’re importing, what we’re not, and why).
Track record of operating in execution-heavy environments with high ownership and high attention to correctness (where mistakes create customer-facing trust issues).
Experience with customer-facing implementation/onboarding work (especially where you need to explain constraints and tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders).

ashby:headway:acfd827b-22f6-4229-aede-ee.summary:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. sections.title: About the Role
paras: NODA AI is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own the products and workflows that turn mission intent into executable plans for autonomous systems. This is a highly technical, customer-facing product role at the intersection of mission planning, command and control, autonomy, and real-world operations. Our users operate in environments where software must do more than be intuitive. It must help operators translate mission intent into executable plans, synchronize actions across systems and platforms, understand risks and constraints, and adapt as conditions change. You will bring a deep understanding of how operators plan and execute missions today and help define how those workflows evolve as autonomous and multi-domain systems become increasingly central to operations. We are looking for someone who understands mission planning software, command-and-control systems, and operational workflows, ideally through direct experience with systems such as Joint Mission Planning System (JMPS), FalconView, Portable Flight Planning Software (PFPS), other comparable DoD mission planning or C2 products, and commercial ground control stations such as QGroundControl.

This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role with significant product ownership. You will spend time with operators, work shoulder-to-shoulder with Engineering and Design, participate in field exercises and customer deployments, and see firsthand how the product performs in operational environments. You will serve as a voice of the operator, translating operator feedback, doctrine, TTPs, field observations, technical constraints and customer requirements into product strategy, intuitive workflows, and engineering priorities. A critical part of this role will be helping NODA AI evolve into a scalable multi-domain product platform. You will identify patterns across missions, customers, platforms, and integrations and determine what should become configurable, repeatable product capability, balancing immediate operational needs and customer commitments with the long-term architecture and integrity of the platform.

This role requires strong product instincts, technical fluency, operational awareness and the ability to bring structure and coordination to ambiguous, cross-functional problems. You will own meaningful product outcomes from discovery through development, field deployment, and iteration. You will help define what we build and why, make difficult prioritization decisions, and distinguish between what a customer asks for and the underlying problem the product should solve. Success requires deep user empathy, technical fluency, strong product and design judgment, and the ability to bring clarity to complex, ambiguous problems. You will partner closely with Engineering to deliver capabilities that reduce operator workload, accelerate decision-making, and give users confidence in the plans they execute when the mission matters.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Facilitate the product strategy, roadmap, and requirements for NODA AI's mission planning software, translating mission needs into intuitive, operationally relevant product capabilities.

Act as the voice of the operator, working directly with warfighters, mission planners, and Government stakeholders to understand operational workflows, identify unmet needs, and translate insights into product direction.

Define and evolve workflows for mission creation, course-of-action development, planning, tasking, coordination, visualization, feasibility validation, execution, monitoring, and dynamic re-planning across autonomous and multi-domain systems.

Translate mission objectives, operator workflows, technical constraints, and customer requirements into clear product requirements, workflows, user stories, acceptance criteria, and development priorities.

Drive the transition from programs to scalable product capabilities, identifying patterns across customer engagements and defining the abstractions, configurations, workflows, and interfaces that turn one-off requirements into repeatable capabilities across customers and missions.

Partner closely with Engineering and Design through the full product lifecycle, from discovery and prototyping through development, integration, field deployment, validation, and iteration, delivering reliable and intuitive experiences that increase operator confidence.
Drive product decisions involving complex interactions between planning software, autonomy, command and control, communications, networking, sensors, payloads, platforms, and Ground Control Stations.
Evaluate integration and interoperability requirements with existing Government systems, mission planning tools, Ground Control Stations, data formats, interfaces, and operational workflows.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We are looking for a seasoned Head of Product to own and scale this function. This is one of the most important hires we will make as a company.

Novellia operates at the intersection of healthcare and consumer, where patient empowerment meets everyday life. We believe the best products in this space feel less like medical tools and more like things people actually want to use. The early team has been driving product decisions since day one. That's gotten us here. Now we need someone to take us from a great foundation and grow the org that carries us through Series B and beyond. Represent product in board conversations, partner discussions, and recruiting

sections.title: About the Role
paras: We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to be our product’s right hand as Osmo scales its Software and AI organization. This is a hands-on product role, not a program management role — you'll own scoping, requirements, and delivery negotiation directly, working independently from day one.

Your first mandate: Osmo's internal workflows are largely manual today, and information doesn't always flow through our systems the way it should. You'll identify the 3-5 tools that would drive 80% of the impact, embed with the relevant teams to master the problem, and come out with clear requirements that get built. From there, expect to move across workstreams as priorities shift, applying the same structural skills to a new domain. You'll work closely with engineering throughout, and you'll need to hold your own there: when an estimate doesn't add up, you push back with specifics, ask for the breakdown, and know how to simplify a requirement to get something shipped faster. This role takes real tenacity to drive scope and delivery under ambiguity, and real kindness in how you ask a stretched engineering team for more.

sections.title: What You'll Do:
bullets: Scope With Rigor — Independently scope projects end to end: understand the business value and customer need, then write clear, complete requirements that inform what engineering builds.

Negotiate Scope and Estimates — When an engineering estimate doesn't match reality, push back with tenacity: ask for the breakdown, identify what's actually driving the cost, and simplify or revise the requirement to get to a faster, leaner build.
Find the 80% — Scope Osmo's highest-value internal tooling opportunities: identify the 3-5 tools that would drive the majority of workflow impact, then sequence and prioritize the build.
Embed and Master — Rapidly insert yourself into a workstream, understand it deeply, and come out with the requirements and plan to fix what's broken.
Partner Directly With Engineering — Work hand-in-hand with the CTO’s team to get scoped work built and delivered against committed dates.

Operate Without a Script — Take high-level direction into an ambiguous space and bring back clarity, milestones, and a plan — with the curiosity to figure out what's actually needed rather than waiting to be told.
Bring Structure Without Bureaucracy — Sequence and manage ambiguous initiatives without adding process for its own sake.
Pivot With the Business — Move fluidly across workstreams as Osmo's priorities shift, applying the same core PM skill set to new problems.

sections.title: Who You Are:
bullets: A Mid-Senior Generalist — You work independently and bring PM best practices without needing to be trained on the fundamentals. You're a generalist, not a specialist: your skills are fungible, and you're comfortable being reassigned to a completely different problem space.

Direct Engineering Collaboration, Non-Negotiable — You have worked hands-on with engineering teams in a prior role. You know how to sit across from an engineering lead, question an estimate, and land on a scope that actually reflects the work.
A Real Requirements Writer — Writing requirements documents has been a core, sustained part of at least one prior role — not a one-off exercise.
Comfortable in Ambiguity — You can take a loosely defined problem and a high-level directive and figure out the rest. You don't need a detailed plan handed to you.

A Clear, Confident Communicator — You can bridge business needs and engineering constraints, and you're comfortable pushing back on senior stakeholders, including leadership, when timelines, scope, or resources don't add up.
An AI-Native Operator — Fluency with modern AI tools (LLMs, automation platforms, workflow builders), with a track record of using them in your own work.
Bachelor's degree or higher, or equivalent experience.

sections.title: Ways to Stand Out:
bullets: You thrive in ambiguity and build your way out of it — We move fast and our pioneering in our space. We build what no one has ever imagined before.
You've Worked Alongside Deep Technical or Scientific Teams — Comfortable partnering with ML, hardware, or R&D-heavy functions even though this is not a technical specialist role.
You've Pivoted Across Domains — You've moved across genuinely different product areas within the same company and ramped quickly each time.
You've Operated at a Small, Fast-Moving Company — Where you had to build the process yourself rather than inherit one.
You Drive Without Authority — You've driven alignment and delivery in a flat org through credibility, not title.
You've Shipped Internal Tooling Before — You've scoped and delivered workflow or internal tooling improvements that measurably reduced manual work or fixed broken information flow.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Ramp believes that AI-powered CX organizations are the future and we are racing to build the best one in the world. Our goal is for our team to work hand in hand with AI agents to drive superlative customer outcomes and the highest-velocity AI improvement engine in the business.

This role will own the strategy and ops teams that are making that transition a reality while still delivering 24/7/365 support for our 85,000+ customers every day. You will work with the Head of CX to set the goals, measure what matters, and build the systems and programs that push the team forward. You’ll manage a small and mighty team across Business Operations, CX Analytics, Workforce Management, Learning & Development, and CX AI Operations to accomplish your goals.

We believe every CX frontline specialist has a role to play driving forward the performance of our AI agents - it is not work reserved for a dedicated AI team. Each specialist needs to be trained, coached, scheduled, and rewarded for continuous work of closing AI learning loops, ensuring AI escalations get resolved, and obsessing about how our customers are actually being served.

bullets: Set the goals and measure what matters. Work with the Head of CX and senior CX managers to set org-wide goals, decide how we measure progress, and deliver the programs and projects that enable that strategy to flourish.
Define how specialists and AI agents work together. Build the roles, workflows, and expectations that let specialists and AI agents serve customers as one team.

Change what we reward. Rebuild goals, incentives, and performance management so specialists get credit for closing AI learning loops, getting AI escalations resolved, and improving how customers are actually served, alongside traditional frontline performance.
Own global schedules, capacity, and quality. Plan coverage for 24/7/365, multi-tier, global support that holds a high bar for customers of all shapes and sizes.

Build the training model for the new work. Both new and tenured specialists need to investigate hard issues, judge agent behavior, and contribute fixes, while still developing a deep understanding Ramp’s complex financial products. L&D should make them good at all of it.

Turn AI progress into operating change. Know what our Investigative Copilot (specialist-facing) and AskRamp (fully agentic) can do and how well they do it. When that moves, change staffing, workflows, training, and expectations to match.

Build and own the voice of the CX specialist to Product and Engineering. Use CX data to show technical teams where agents succeed and where they struggle, and work with them directly on tooling, prompts, and agent behavior. They own the roadmap; you make sure CX's evidence shapes it.

Build a small, strong team. Develop and grow leaders across Business Operations, CX Analytics, Workforce Management, Learning & Development, and CX AI Operations, with clear ownership and shared goals.

You'll need to learn the product fast, build fast, and use AI tools to scale yourself so one person can support a team that keeps growing. ashby:sola:ba78cc55-723a-4d4b-93ad-56535.summary:

Sola is an AI-native platform reinventing enterprise process automation and disrupting legacy RPA tools. sections.title: About the role
paras: Anthropic's consulting and systems integration partners now sell and deliver Claude work at growing volume, and selling alongside partners is working. What matters next is delivery: whether the partner completes the work, whether the customer's Claude usage grows and holds, and whether the outcome is good enough that the customer asks for that partner again.

The Partner Success Lead owns that outcome. You will hold a book of in-flight customer engagements across a set of managed partners in North America. From the day our Partner Delivery program matches a customer engagement to a partner in your book, you own it to a completed outcome: the work finishes on scope, the customer's Claude usage grows, and a stalled engagement gets diagnosed and unblocked before the customer disengages. You wake up every day on one question: what is each partner in my book doing, and is the work getting done.

sections.title: Key responsibilities:
bullets: Own every customer engagement in your book from partner match to completed outcome. Know the state of each one every week: scope, timeline, blockers, and the customer's Claude usage trend.

Run the weekly delivery review across your book, and bring stalled or at-risk engagements to the weekly at-risk account review with a diagnosis, an owner, and a specific ask rather than a status list.

Unblocking. Partner capacity, scope creep, customer readiness, product questions, deal-registration conflicts, and customer dissatisfaction with partner work: get each issue to the right internal team and stay on it through resolution.

Own delivery quality and consumption across your book. Track engagements completed on time, time from match to completion, delivered consumption and weekly active use on the customer accounts your partners serve, and the accounts trending toward at-risk.

Build senior relationships with each managed partner's practice and delivery leadership. Together with the Partner Account Manager and other Anthropic counterparts, establish the executive-level trust that lets you ask a partner to restaff, escalate, or invest — and be taken seriously — when an engagement needs it.

Build each partner's Claude practice as the compounding work: certified bench depth, one repeatable offering in a chosen industry lane, and a published customer story from each completed engagement, so the next engagement needs less from you.

Turn what works into methodology. Convert the moves you prove in your book into named, reusable best practices — engagement review packs, unblocking plays, practice-building guides — written clearly enough to be shared at scale across partners, the Partner Success team, and the contract delivery team running the same loop.

Run the quarterly practice review with each managed partner's alliance and delivery leads: joint goals on completed customer engagements, customer adoption, certified practitioners, references, and industry positioning.

sections.title: Minimum qualifications:
bullets: Experience owning a high-volume book of concurrent customer engagements, projects, or accounts (roughly 10 to 30 at a time) to completed outcomes, in a partner success, customer success, delivery management, or technical account management role.

Track record of a number tied to completed work and customer behavior (on-time delivery, adoption, retention, consumption, expansion) rather than contract signature, and an operating rhythm you built to hit it.

Judgment on delivery quality: you can review a partner's engagement plan or scope and tell whether it will finish on time and produce usage, and you ask the follow-up question that surfaces the real risk.

Escalation and unblocking judgment across a matrix (partner, customer, direct sales, customer success, product): you know which stall belongs to whom, you get help fast, and you stay engaged to resolution.

A convincing speaker and presenter to all kinds of audiences: partner executives, delivery practitioners, customers, and internal leadership. You can carry a quarterly practice review, an enablement session, and an executive escalation in the same week and land each one.
Deep understanding of how customer success works in a usage-based business; you have held a number tied to customer behavior and can read a consumption trend and act on it.

Enough technical fluency to be credible in a delivery review. You do not need to write code, but you can follow a partner architect's walkthrough of a real Claude engagement and ask the substantive second question.

Active daily use of Claude or another large language model as part of how you work: preparing reviews, drafting account plans, and analyzing your book. We will ask you to walk us through a recent deliverable.

The read on the account. You understand their supply chain and their business well enough to find the openings they have not told us about yet.

In this role, you’ll manage and develop a team of Customer Success leaders and Customer Success Managers, establish operating rhythms and scalable processes, and partner cross-functionally with Sales, Implementation, and Product to ensure customers realize measurable value from Dealpath. Ensure high-quality enablement and training experiences (virtual and in-person) that drive adoption across complex customer teams.

Standardize processes for renewals, expansion identification, playbook execution, and executive communications.
Improve cross-functional workflows and SLAs across Implementation, Product, and Sales.

sections.title: Cross-functional leadership and customer advocacy
bullets: Partner with Sales leadership on expansion strategy, process alignment, and smooth account transitions.
Partner with Product and Engineering to surface customer feedback, influence roadmap priorities, and reduce recurring friction points.
Represent the voice of the customer internally and ensure issues are prioritized appropriately.

greenhouse:ethoslife:8859340002.summary: Ethos (Nasdaq: $LIFE) is a leading life insurance technology company on a mission to protect families by democratizing access to life insurance and empowering agents at scale. With its robust three-sided technology platform, Ethos is transforming the life insurance experience for consumers, agents, and carriers alike. Ethos offers instant, accessible products and a seamless online process that requires no medical exams and just a few health questions; it eliminates traditional barriers, making it easier than ever for everyone to protect their families. Ethos is redefining how life insurance is bought, sold, and underwritten.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Ethos has digitized one of the most painful journeys in consumer finance. Today, someone can apply for life insurance in minutes, with no medical exam and just a few health questions. Our digital experience is highly functional; now we want to make it inspirational, educational, and genuinely helpful at the moments that matter most.

We’re looking for an exceptional Product leader to own the back half of our consumer funnel: the health interview where users answer sensitive questions and get an instant underwriting decision and the post-approval experience where they choose how much coverage they need, for how long, and complete their purchase. These are the highest-stakes moments in the journey, where trust, clarity, and confidence determine whether a family ends up protected. Your work will have a direct and positive impact on people’s lives at scale.

This is a role for a senior product leader who pairs first-principles thinking and deep consumer empathy with rigorous experimentation and a talent for simplifying complexity. Ethos is a product-first company, and Product leaders (as well as PMs) here operate with a high degree of ownership.You'll lead a team of product managers, set the multi-year vision for these surfaces, drive your team’s quarterly planning and roadmap, and be accountable for results at scale.

greenhouse:formic:4726483006.summary:
Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.

We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.

sections.title: Who we are:
paras: Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.

sections.title: About the Customer Success team:
paras: Customer Success is dedicated to enabling our customers to get the most out of the automation we deploy, facilitating a superb experience through all facets of our relationship. We are manufacturing and automation experts–consulting with customers to drive adoption and optimal usage of our robotic automation solutions, and identifying opportunities to continue their automation journey.

As Customer Success Manager , you will serve as the primary point of contact and advisory partner for our customers: visiting and consulting with those customers in the field, and driving solutions across various groups within Formic for optimal delivery of technical, operational, training and administrative support for our industrial robot systems.

You will play a key role in driving mutually beneficial customer relationships post-deployment by monitoring customer health and engagement, mitigating potential relationship and experience risks, and identifying growth opportunities in existing accounts. You will build and maintain strong customer relationships; develop a deep understanding of their business goals, challenges, and needs; and will leverage that feedback to provide customized insights and value-added products and services. This position is highly strategic and impactful in Formic’s mission to be a valued partner and leader driving the adoption of automation across the manufacturing industry.

sections.title: As Customer Success Manager, you will:
bullets: Serve as the primary consultative partner and point of contact for the group of customers you are responsible for: building strong relationships; facilitating technical, operational, training, and administrative support; and identifying opportunities for expansion.

Oversee a regular cadence of communication and site visits (including regular travel throughout your region) to assess satisfaction with deployed robotic automation systems, address relationship issues, facilitate and offer training, solicit feedback, and identify opportunities for growth and improvement.
Monitor & manage health and engagement by using diagnostic tools and strategic communication, identifying and mitigating potential relationship and experience risks.
Collaborate with Formic’s Sales, Deployment, and Service teams to guide customers - particularly first time automation buyers - through their automation journey.
Identify opportunities for growth of products and services within existing accounts, including deployment of additional like-for-like solutions, or upstream or downstream standard solutions.
Leverage understanding of customers’ businesses to provide feedback for new product offerings and service enhancements for Formic to better serve their needs.

Familiarity with robotic automation systems in a manufacturing or production environment (e.g. robotic automation of palletizing, de-palletizing, case packing, machine tending, welding, injection molding).
Outstanding communication and stakeholder management skills–able to build trusting relationships with diverse stakeholders and audiences and collaborate cross-functionally

Ability to identify expansion opportunities through strong relationships, customer insight, and operational outcomes
Proficiency with CRM and customer relationship management tools such as Salesforce, ticketing systems, or project tracking platforms

Experience working with industrial, manufacturing, hardware, robotics, or operationally complex customers preferred

Partnering closely with Motive's AI Safety and computer vision teams, you'll turn complex safety signals into clear, trusted, and actionable workflows, including agentic experiences that surface the events that matter most and help customers act faster.

greenhouse:instacart:8257641.summary:
At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

sections.title: Instacart is a Flex First team
paras: There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. paras: The Customer Experience (CX) team sits at the center of Instacart’s support ecosystem, serving our diverse community of consumers, shoppers, retailers, and advertisers through both direct support and scalable solutions. We partner closely with cross-functional teams across Product, Engineering, and Operations to surface insights from the front line, reduce friction in the customer journey, and shape future roadmaps.

We deliver empathetic, high-quality support through a blend of data-driven, operational excellence. By focusing on clear communication, critical thinking, and continuous improvement, we ensure that every customer interaction not only resolves the immediate issue but also consistently enhances the overall Instacart experience.

paras: Ketryx is an AI software platform that enables healthcare life sciences companies to ship life-saving regulated products in weeks instead of years.

Since launch, Ketryx already touches the lives of 100M patients and powers all of the world's top five medical device manufacturers. Backed by Lightspeed Ventures, our founders are the former Head of AI at Amgen and CTO of Wolfram Cloud.

greenhouse:kikoff:4520824009.summary:
Kikoff: The Fintech Powering Financial Security at Scale
Kikoff is a profitable, pre-IPO fintech company on a mission to empower everyone to achieve financial security. With record revenue growth in 2025 and a unicorn valuation, we've built a suite of products that help millions of people build credit, access liquidity, and save money.
We're scaling fast. Join us if you want to build something meaningful and help millions of people move forward financially.

sections.title: Why Kikoff:
paras: This is a consumer fintech startup, and you will be working with serial entrepreneurs who have built strong consumer brands and innovative products. We value extreme ownership, clear communication, a strong sense of craftsmanship, and the desire to create lasting work and work relationships. Yes, you can build an exciting business AND have real-life real-customer impact.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We are looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to lead the strategic narrative and inbound go-to-market engine for Kikoff—the #1 credit-building app. Having empowered over 1 million customers on their financial journeys, we are now entering a phase of rapid portfolio expansion.

This is a high-impact role for a seasoned PMM who thrives in the "upstream." You won’t just be launching features; you will be an essential partner to the Product organization, shaping what we build next through exploratory research and validating product-market fit for entirely new concepts. This is your opportunity to build the scalable systems that define how a category-leader wins.

sections.title: In this role you will:
bullets: Architect the Strategic Narrative: You will lead the development of the foundational messaging frameworks and positioning for our product suite. You'll ensure our story is differentiated, defensible, and resonates deeply with the financial aspirations of millions.

Drive Inbound Strategy & Exploration: You will spearhead exploratory work to identify market signals before products are built. You’ll oversee customer discovery, conduct deep-dive interviews, and translate ambiguous pain points into concrete product roadmaps.

Build Strategic Moats: You will drive the design and execution of rigorous experiments to optimize pricing, packaging, and positioning. Your work will deliver measurable lifts in activation and monetization, ensuring our products are as commercially viable as they are impactful.

Act as the Cross-Functional Connective Tissue: You will align diverse teams—Product, Growth, Design, Data, and Creative—around the highest-impact opportunities. You'll drive follow-through across dependencies and resolve organizational gaps to protect outcomes.

Scale a World-Class Team: You will manage and mentor a growing team of Product Marketers. Your focus will be on "talent architecture"—coaching experienced ICs through strategic hurdles while building a strong development pipeline for junior talent.

Establish Repeatable Excellence: You won't just solve problems; you'll build the playbooks. You will create the frameworks that make high-quality product marketing repeatable and scalable as we transition from a single product to a multi-faceted financial ecosystem.

sections.title: What will make you successful:
paras: A note on applying: We know great candidates sometimes hold back if they don’t meet every qualification listed. If you’re excited about this role and believe you can do the work, we encourage you to apply. We’re looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.
Please reference the following for more information .
bullets: A Proven Track Record: You have 5+ years of experience in Product Marketing

Sharp Inbound Instincts: You are most energized by the "blank page" phase of a project. you know how to turn raw customer insights into a winning product strategy and can validate demand through creative testing.

Strategic Ownership: You don’t wait for a roadmap—you define it. You are comfortable shaping priorities, making hard trade-offs, and communicating them clearly to senior leadership with both candor and care.
Analytical Rigor: You default to testing over assuming. You are fluent in data and use it to sharpen your intuition on positioning, pricing, and product direction.
Executive Presence: You have the ability to navigate high-growth environments, build trust with stakeholders you don't manage, and influence the company's "True North."
Mission Alignment: You are genuinely passionate about financial health. You understand that Kikoff succeeds only when our customers achieve their financial goals.
Relevant Sector Experience: You have a background in Fintech, Consumer Finance, or high-growth B2C. Familiarity with credit, lending, or highly regulated products is a significant plus.

greenhouse:medicalinformaticsengineering.summary:
Enterprise Health is seeking a Product Manager who brings firsthand understanding of occupational health, employee health, or third-party occupational health (3POH), along with the product management skills to turn that knowledge into better software. The ideal candidate understands the people, programs, and business realities behind workplace health—not just the technology used to document care.

This role will lead discovery, prioritization, and product outcomes across important workflows such as medical surveillance, employee health compliance and immunizations, workplace injury and case management, return-to-work, and employer-provider coordination. Areas of product ownership may evolve with customer needs and portfolio strategy.

sections.title: Primary Responsibility 1: Domain-Led Product Strategy & Discovery
bullets: Lead discovery with employee health teams, occupational health clinics, employer health and safety leaders, and 3POH providers to identify operational pain points and unmet needs.
Map real-world workflows from employer requests or employee encounters through service delivery, follow-up, work status, compliance, and reporting.
Understand the roles, incentives, constraints, and buying dynamics of employers, health systems, and occupational medicine providers.
Define product opportunities, hypotheses, and roadmap priorities grounded in customer evidence, market needs, strategic fit, and business value.
Identify opportunities to reduce manual work, improve compliance and coordination, and make multi-party workflows easier to manage.
Use customer interviews, workflow observation, prototypes, and data to validate problems and proposed solutions before committing to delivery.
Assess where AI and automation can create differentiated, measurable value in workplace health workflows.

sections.title: Primary Responsibility 2: Product Development & Delivery
bullets: Own assigned capabilities end-to-end, from discovery and business case through delivery, launch, adoption, measurement, and iteration.
Partner with Engineering and Design to turn validated problems into intuitive, scalable experiences for clinicians, program administrators, employers, and external providers.
Apply domain judgment to balance clinical, compliance, operational, usability, technical, and commercial needs.
Coordinate across Product Managers and teams to deliver connected workflows across the Enterprise Health platform.
Simplify complex workflows while preserving the configurability, reliability, and controls required by enterprise customers.
Prototype and deliver AI-enabled or automated capabilities when evidence supports meaningful customer and business impact.

sections.title: Primary Responsibility 3: Commercialization & Adoption
bullets: Collaborate with Product Marketing, Sales, Client Success, and implementation teams on positioning, launches, enablement, and sustained adoption.
Define outcomes and KPIs such as time saved, fewer manual steps, service turnaround, compliance, adoption, and customer value.
Use product data and customer feedback to evaluate results and continuously improve workflow effectiveness.
Understand competitive alternatives—including manual processes, point solutions, and occupational health platforms—and communicate differentiated value.

We’re building an engaging marketplace where users trade on real-world outcomes - from major sports and elections to cultural and financial events. With a sleek mobile-first app and a passionate community, we’re redefining how people interact with news, probabilities, and financial markets. OG.com runs on the rails of North American Derivatives Exchange, Inc. (NADEX), a CFTC-regulated exchange operating since 2004 and was acquired by crypto.com in 2022.

sections.title: Role Overview
paras: We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the consumer prediction-market trading experience end-to-end - web and mobile - once someone can fund: discovery, order entry, positions, parlays / live, and the fan UX that makes OG the default place to trade on real-world outcomes.

Your mandate is to make OG fast, clear, and design-obsessive for sports and prediction users: the core trading surfaces that keep them coming back, the workflows that feel native to fans (and to retail traders), and the translation of that craft into regulated U.S. event contracts. Fiat, KYC, and payment rails sit with a partner PM. You own what they do after they’re funded.

You will run this roadmap with independence. You make the call on UX tradeoffs, what ships when design quality isn’t there yet, and which trading patterns we borrow from sportsbooks, prediction apps, or retail perps -and which we refuse. You report to the Chief Product Officer, who sets product strategy and priorities across OG. You own the how and the when.
bullets: Native consumer predictions - sports fluency, parlays / live, fan UX - and you can bridge that into regulated event contracts.
Prediction / event markets -you’ve already shipped this category.
Retail perps / derivatives / advanced trading -you know trader-grade workflows and can make them accessible for fans, not only power users.

If you’ve shipped any of those, this will feel familiar. The difference is you’ll be doing it in regulated U.S. prediction markets -where sports energy, consumer accessibility, and compliance collide, and the playbook for “best consumer trading experience in the category” is yours to write.

sections.title: What You'll Actually Do:
bullets: Own the consumer trading roadmap. You are the DRI for web and mobile trading on OG -from first funded session through confident, repeat use. You set milestones, sequence work, and resolve cross-team dependencies. Nothing in this charter goes live without your sign-off on product and UX bar.

Ship the product fans actually use. You prioritize market discovery, order entry, positions, parlays / multi-leg, live, and the workflows that keep sports and prediction users engaged. You kill “nice ideas” that don’t move outcomes.

Bridge native prediction (or perps) into regulated event contracts. You take patterns fans already know -sportsbooks, prediction apps, or retail advanced trading -and make them work under U.S. event-contract rules. You don’t copy a sportsbook blindly. You decide what translates.

Hold the design bar. You champion usability and aesthetics as non-negotiable. You live in design reviews and give specific, actionable UX feedback -spacing, interaction patterns, information density, not vibes. Fan UX is a product skill, not a polish pass.
Wireframe and partner in Figma. You create your own wires and drive design conversations. You catch pixel misalignments and clunky trade flows before users do.

Talk to users like a peer. You run research, interviews, and community feedback. You ask “Show me how you currently place this parlay / live bet / perp,” not “Would you use this feature?” You distinguish what users say from what their behavior reveals.

Drive cross-functional execution. You align engineering, design, data, compliance, and ops around trading outcomes. You partner with the Fiat/Onboarding PM on funded → first contract. You own the backlog and the ship cadence for trading.

sections.title: Requirements:
bullets: Sports fluency or trader-to-fan translation. Either you already speak fan (games, legs, live, why UX has to be instant) or you have taken complex trading UX and made it usable for a broader retail audience -and you can show the before/after.

Design sensibility as a product skill. You can evaluate and improve UI/UX with specifics (hierarchy, density, interaction cost), not “it looks nicer.” You can point to a product users loved because of craft, and what you refused to ship.
Data ownership. You instrument your own funnel, size the opportunity, and prioritize without waiting for someone to hand you the analysis.
User empathy in the product. You are willing to use OG regularly (discover markets, trade, manage positions) to feel friction firsthand. You ask behavioral questions before feature questions.
We care what you’ve built and owned -not MBA, pedigree, or a certain number of years.

sections.title: Preferred:
bullets: Hands-on prediction-market or sports-trading as a user: accelerates ramp on parlays, live markets, and what fans expect.
You’ve done more than one of the three worlds (e.g. sportsbook + prediction, or perps + consumer app): you ramp faster on what to steal and what to leave behind.
Fiat / onboarding familiarity: helpful so you respect the funded → first-trade handoff. Not required -a partner PM owns rails.
Deep Figma / design-system fluency: you move faster with design as a peer, not a handoff.
AI player and pilot: you use AI tools with human-in-the-loop judgment to move faster on research, specs, and iteration.

Protect Democracy seeks a highly motivated, organized Legislative & Advocacy Specialist who is passionate about building a more representative, responsive, and resilient democracy by advancing policy solutions and supporting overall federal advocacy efforts. The Specialist will work in collaboration with others in and outside of the organization to coordinate and administer outreach to congressional offices, committees, and others. Ideal candidates for this position have experience working within Congress, federal government affairs, or a similar role. Candidates must also have demonstrated experience and interest working in cross-ideological coalitions in order to build broad support on a particular issue.

Protect Democracy was formed in late 2016 with an urgent and explicit mission: to prevent our democracy from declining into a more authoritarian form of government. We have since…

sections.title: Legislative & Advocacy Specialist (2026)
paras: Joining our organization as a Legislative & Advocacy Specialist is an excellent opportunity to make a generational impact on our democracy at a time when core checks and balances and the rule of law are being challenged, and American people are hungry for change. Candidates who are eager to learn new issue areas quickly and have the ability to pivot workstreams when current events unfold are strongly encouraged to apply.
This is a hybrid position based in Washington, DC.*

At Protect Democracy, we believe that diversity isn’t just a strength — it’s a necessity for tackling the complex challenges facing democracy. A broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and lived experiences strengthen our ability to analyze problems, craft solutions, and drive meaningful change. We strongly encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds and from across the political and ideological spectrum to apply. If you meet most but not all of the criteria listed below but believe nonetheless you’d be a stellar match for the role and could grow into it, we want to hear from you.

sections.title: The Legislative & Advocacy Specialist will:
bullets: Build trusting and productive relationships with congressional offices and partners across the political spectrum and advocacy ecosystem to advance our organizational priorities;
Track and catalogue legislative outreach across the organization to maximize impact and ensure seamless, effective coordination across teams;
Work with members of Congress, their staffs, agency leaders, experts, and coalition partners to advance pro-democracy legislative reforms;
Design and develop creative, forward-looking policy proposals, memos and explainers (such as this and this ) and work with legislators, agencies, experts, and coalitions to advance them;

Partner with colleagues across the organization to proactively issue spot and deconflict outreach and to develop integrated advocacy approaches that combine policy advocacy and communications strategies to bring about change.

sections.title: To be successful in this role, you should have:
bullets: Three or more years of relevant professional experience, including at least one year of experience working on the Hill or in federal legislative advocacy;
Demonstrated ability to build trusting and productive relationships with partners across the political spectrum and ecosystem;
Ability to communicate ideas, concepts and policy solutions;
Ability to draft concrete policy proposals, including legislative text and supporting policy documents;.
Ability to write persuasive and accessible policy analysis, articles, memos, and reports;
Excellent political judgment, including the ability to determine what levers can make change happen with limited resources;
Growth mindset and enthusiasm for giving and receiving feedback up, down, and sideways;

A passionate commitment to strengthening democratic norms and institutions, an understanding that our democracy has never fully represented communities of color, and unfettered enthusiasm for Protect Democracy’s cross-ideological and nonpartisan approach .

sections.title: Preferred, not required:
bullets: Experience with Quorum or any other CRM.

sections.title: Additional Information
paras:
A Quick Note Before You Apply…

Cricut is in a powerful chapter of transformation. We’re evolving fast—refining our strategy, growing our teams, and raising the bar across the board. This is an incredible opportunity for the right kind of person—but it’s not for everyone.

We’re looking for A-players —people who don’t just meet expectations, but consistently exceed them. If you thrive in dynamic environments and find joy in turning challenges into momentum, keep reading.

Here’s what makes someone a great fit for this role (and for this moment at Cricut):

You have a bias for urgency.

You don’t wait for perfect clarity to take action—you start, learn, and adjust. You believe that speed matters, especially when paired with thoughtfulness. You ask: “What can move forward today?” and push past inertia.

You set high standards—especially for yourself.

You’re proud of your work and protective of your reputation. You take ownership, deliver quality, and don’t cut corners. You hold yourself accountable without waiting to be asked.

You stay focused when things are moving fast.

You can identify what really matters and don’t get distracted by noise. You prioritize well, and manage your time wisely.

You collaborate like a pro.

You elevate the people around you, communicate clearly, and give thoughtful feedback. You’re low ego, high output—and your team loves working with you.
